answer.evidence: The sprite is a 15px-wide, 14-row near-rectangular patch (rows 1-14 are all width 15, rows 0 and 15 narrower at 8) with soft yellow/orange light tones (#fff8b0, #efdd7d, #ffd8a0, #f4b370) blended irregularly. No front-edge line, no eave shadow, no vertical face, and no standing volume. It is a flat ground decal seen from above, so there is no front face (0 rows). That matches the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours in total and a median of 4 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and 26 per tile, and even the simple paving reference has 7 distinct colours and 7 per tile. The candidate shows a faint speckle with no flat 5x5 blocks (0% coverage), but the speckle is built from only about 3 lightness steps, against 5-6 for Beodeul materials. It has no outline, and its edge pixels are not neutral, so it is not a black-line sticker. There are no clumps, no grain in several tones and no per-element shading, which is what makes the reference tiles information-rich. It would look thin and flat next to the grass ground. Soft light patches can be low-colour, but this is below even the paving reference on colour count and tonal variety.
